extracted.intended_audience: users/developers of SINGULAR (computational algebra / algebraic geometry practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of SINGULAR library procedures: for each procedure it gives usage signature, assumptions, return values, purpose/behavior, optional arguments, and examples. Audience are SINGULAR users who call these library routines for computational algebra tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReesAlgebra
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ReesAlgebra(I); I = ideal. Return: The Rees algebra R[It] as an affine ring, returned as a list of two rings: [1] a ring RR containing an ideal ker such that R[It] = RR/ker; [2] a ring Kxt (the basering with additional variable t) containing an ideal mapI defining the map RR -> Kxt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute the Rees algebra. Example shows LIB "reesclos.lib"; ring R=0,(x,y),dp; ideal I= x2,xy4,y5; list L=ReesAlgebra(I); Rees=L[1]; setring Rees; ker lists generators. Notes: output contains rings and kernel ideal; inspect ker and ring to get isomorphism R[It] ≃ Rees/ker.

rubrics_metrics.name: normalI
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: normalI(I[, p [, r [, l]]]); I an ideal, p,r,l optional integers. Return: a list containing closures of desired powers of I as ideals of the basering. Computes integral closure of I^p (and optionally multiple powers); if p omitted or p==0, computes closure of all powers up to max degree in t occurring in closure of R[It].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior: starts by checking if I is radical. If l==1 uses locNormal instead of normal. If r==1 behavior about which powers is explained (closure not just sum/product of smaller). Display verbosity depends on printlevel. Example given with LIB "reesclos.lib"; ring and ideal, then list J = normalI(I).

rubrics_metrics.name: sagbiSPoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sagbiSPoly(A[, returnRing, meth]); A is an ideal; returnRing and meth optional integers. Return: ideal or ring. Purpose: returns SAGBI S-polynomials of the leading terms of A if returnRing=0; otherwise returns a new ring containing ideals algebraicRelations and spolynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering is not a qring. Optional meth argument chooses method for computing algebraic relations: meth=0 (default) uses std, meth=1 uses slimgb, meth=2 uses toric ideal. Example shows computing spolynomials and algebraicRelations and verifying substitution. Use returnRing=1 to get extended ring with stored objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: sagbiReduce
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sagbiReduce(I, A[, tr, mt]); I, A ideals, tr (tailred) and mt optional integers. Return: ideal of remainders of I after SAGBI reduction by A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering is not a qring. tr determines tail reduction: tr=0 => no tail reduction; tr<>0 => do tail reduction. mt determines Groebner method: mt=0 (default) => std; mt=1 => slimgb. Example shows reduction of polynomials with and without tail reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: sagbi
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sagbi(A[, tr, mt]); A ideal, tr and mt optional integers. Return: an ideal, a SAGBI basis for A. Purpose: computes a SAGBI basis for subalgebra generated by A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering is not a qring. tr (tailred): 0 no tail reduction, <>0 perform tail reduction. mt: method for Groebner computations (0 std, 1 slimgb). Examples: default call returns generators; call with tail reduction may change output.

rubrics_metrics.name: sagbiPart
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sagbiPart(A, k[, tr, mt]); A is an ideal, k, tr, mt integers. Return: ideal. Purpose: performs k iterations of the SAGBI construction algorithm for the subalgebra generated by A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering is not a qring. tr controls tail reduction as above; mt controls Groebner method. Note: algorithm may not terminate in finite SAGBI basis; the procedure stops after k iterations and returns current generators (which may not be a SAGBI basis). Examples show behavior for 2 and 3 iterations and warning messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: algebraicDependence
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: algebraicDependence(I, it); I ideal, it integer (number of iterations). Return: ring containing ideal algDep with possible algebraic dependencies of elements of I obtained through it iterations of SAGBI construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering is not a qring. Purpose: detect dependencies via SAGBI construction. Example: call with different iteration counts, inspect algDep; use map/substitution to verify dependencies. Output may show no dependency (algDep[1]=0) or actual dependencies after substitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: markov4ti2
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: markov4ti2(A[, i]); A = intmat, i optional int. Return: the toric ideal specified by the Markov basis thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumptions: A is an integer matrix; if second argument omitted A describes lattice as ker(A); if second argument positive, A is interpreted as left image Im(A) = {zA}. Number of variables in basering must equal columns of A (for ker(A)) or rows of A (for Im(A)). Creates temporary files sing4ti2.mat, .lat, .mar for communication with external 4ti2. Input rules for 4ti2 apply (ker(A)={x|Ax=0} and Im(A)={zA}). Example shows two calls with matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: hilbert4ti2
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: hilbert4ti2(A[, i]); A=intmat, i optional. Return: toric ideal specified by Hilbert basis thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumptions similar to markov4ti2: A describes ker(A) or Im(A) depending on second argument; number of basering variables must match. Note: creates temporary files for 4ti2 and requires system tools. Example demonstrates computing Hilbert basis toric generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: graver4ti2
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: graver4ti2(A[, i]); A=intmat, i optional. Return: toric ideal specified by Graver basis thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumptions same as other sing4ti2 interface procedures. Creates temporary I/O files for 4ti2. Example shows returned generators corresponding to Graver basis elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: genSymId
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: genSymId(I, sigma); I ideal, sigma intvec. Return: ideal J such that sigma(J) = J and J includes I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: size(sigma) = nvars(basering) = n. Note: sigma is permutation of variables sigma: var(i) -> var(sigma[i]). Purpose: generate an ideal invariant under sigma by closing set of generators under sigma; can always be obtained by adding sigma(fi) to generator set. Example shows computing symmetric closure for a 5-variable ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: isSymmetric
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isSymmetric(I, sigma); I ideal, sigma intvec. Return: 1 if set of generators of I is invariant under sigma; 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: size(sigma) = nvars(basering). Note: tests whether generator set is invariant (not necessarily ideal equality). Example calls show output 1 or 0 depending on invariance of generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: primRoot
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primRoot(p, k); p,k integers. Assume: p prime and k divides p-1. Return: int, a k-th primitive root of unity in Z/pZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: obtain primitive roots required by modular/symmetric algorithms. Examples show computing primitive roots and checking powers equal 1. Note: used by symmetrization algorithms requiring k-th roots in finite fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: eigenvalues
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: eigenvalues(I, sigma); I ideal, sigma intvec. Assume: size(sigma)=nvars(basering). Return: list of eigenvalues of generators of I under permutation sigma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: sigma permutation acts on variables; eigenvalues correspond to how generators transform. Example demonstrates list of integer eigenvalues for given ideal and permutation.

rubrics_metrics.name: symmStd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: symmStd(I, sigma, #); I ideal, sigma intvec. Assume: sigma(I)=I and basering has an order(sigma)-th primitive root of unity a (if char(basering)>0). Return: an ideal, a standard basis of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: assuming invariance under sigma and existence of primitive root, uses linear transformation to improve standard basis computation; if char(basering)=0 computations done over smallest field extension having requisite root. Example: computing symmetric standard bases for cyclic ideals; returns a (possibly larger) standard basis exploiting symmetry. Note behavior in different characteristics and field extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: syModStd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: syModStd(I, sigma[, #]); I ideal, sigma intvec, optional parameter vector # (1..4 integers). Assume: size(sigma)=nvars(basering) and sigma(I)=I; if size(#)>0 entries control processors and exactness. Return: an ideal, a standard basis of I (if no warning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute standard basis over Q using modular methods and symmetry. Optional vector #: #[1]=number of processors; #[2]=exactness flag (1 => compute for sure, 0 => high probability); #[3]=#primes until first lifting; #[4]=#primes between liftings. Procedure distinguishes variants depending on homogeneity and ordering (variants enumerated 1..4). Examples show usage and comparisons showing zero size reduce between two outputs, demonstrating correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: toric_ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: toric_ideal(A, alg) or toric_ideal(A, alg, prsv); A intmat, alg string, prsv intvec optional. Return: ideal, standard basis of toric ideal of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: returns standard basis of toric ideal of matrix A with respect to current term ordering. Supported algorithms: ect (Conti/Traverso), pt (Pottier), blr (Bigatti/La Scala/Robbiano), hs (Hosten/Sturmfels), du (DiBiase/Urbanke). If alg=blr or hs, algorithm needs a positive vector in row space of A; prsv can supply such vector if no positive row exists. Not all term orderings supported (global orders ok, but not block orderings combining them). Example shows call and error message if positive vector missing; calling with prsv works.

rubrics_metrics.name: toric_std
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: toric_std(I); I ideal. Return: ideal: standard basis of I computed using specialized Buchberger algorithm for toric/binomial ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute standard basis of toric ideals (input generating system should be binomials x^u - x^v). There is no strong check if I is toric: if input consists of binomials but is not toric, toric_std computes an ideal between I and its saturation. Warnings produced if generators are not binomials or monomials not relatively prime. Examples compare toric_std output to std and saturation; demonstrates limitations and warnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incl
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Incl(ideal I, ideal J); I, J ideals. Return: t=1 if variety defined by I contains variety defined by J, otherwise t=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: numerical test for inclusion of algebraic varieties using NumAlg.lib (requires Bertini). Example demonstrates Inclusion: 0 or 1 outputs for given I,J. Note dependencies: Bertini must be installed; library has stated issues (naming, syntax in examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Equal(ideal I, ideal J); I, J ideals. Return: t=1 if variety defined by I equals variety defined by J, otherwise t=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: numerical equality test of varieties. Example shows outputs Equality: 0 or 1 for given ideals. Note reliance on numerical methods and Bertini; examples in documentation show expected output format.

rubrics_metrics.name: DegreePure
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: DegreePure(ideal I, int i); I ideal, i positive integer. Return: the degree of the pure i-dimensional component of the algebraic variety defined by I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute degree of a specific-dimensional component numerically. Example shows Degree of component outputs. Note: requires Bertini and numerical routines; documentation flags syntax/example issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: NumLocalDim
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: NumLocalDim(ideal J, list w, int e); J ideal, w list approximate point v in variety V(J), e integer (precision/complex precision parameter). Return: local dimension of variety defined by J at v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: numerically estimate local dimension at approximate point v using Bertini; examples show local dimensions 0,1,2 for different sample points. Note ring must be complex with precision parameter; need Bertini installed.

rubrics_metrics.name: re2squ
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: re2squ(ideal I); I ideal. Return: ideal J defined by a polynomial system having the same number of polynomials and unknowns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: convert (possibly rectangular) system into square system suitable for numerical solvers. Example: ring/ideal given then def D=re2squ(I); setring D; J shows converted system.

rubrics_metrics.name: UseBertini
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: UseBertini(ideal H, string sv); H ideal, sv string of variables of ring. Return: text file called input used by Bertini to compute solutions of homotopy function H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Need to define a start solution of H. Purpose: prepare input files for Bertini. Example shows building sv=varstr(basering) and def A=UseBertini(I, sv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Singular2bertini
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Singular2bertini(list L); L a list. Return: text file called start. Purpose: adopt list L as a start solution for Bertini homotopy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows calling Singular2bertini with complex start solutions to produce start files for Bertini. Used in workflow coupling Singular and Bertini.

rubrics_metrics.name: bertini2Singular
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: bertini2Singular(string snp, int q); snp string, q = nvars(basering) integer. Return: re list of solutions of homotopy function computed by Bertini.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: read Bertini output (e.g., 'nonsingular_solutions') and import solutions back into Singular as a list. Example demonstrates calling bertini2Singular and retrieving re; requires matching variable counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReJunkUseHomo
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ReJunkUseHomo(ideal I, ideal L, list W, list w); I ideal; L list of generic linear polynomials {l1,...,li}; W list of subset of solution set of generic slicing V(L) with V(J); w list point in V(J). Return: t=1 if w lies on an i-dimensional component of V(I), otherwise t=0 (i = size(L)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: test whether a candidate point w lies on a component of specified dimension using witness sets/slicing. Example shows constructing L, W and calling ReJunkUseHomo and checking result. Notes: requires numerical witness sets produced by Bertini integration (NumDecom workflow).

rubrics_metrics.name: JuReTopDim
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: JuReTopDim(ideal I, list w, int d, int ...?); Return: t=1 if w on a d-dimensional component of V(I), otherwise t=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: test membership of a point in a component of particular dimension (top-dimension). Example calls JuReTopDim(J, w, 2, 2) with output t. Details: used within numerical decomposition procedures; documentation gives example usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: JuReZeroDim
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: JuReZeroDim(ideal I, list w, int ???); Return: t=1 if w lies on a positive-dimensional component of V(I) (i.e., w is not an isolated point), otherwise t=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: distinguish non-isolated vs isolated solutions using numerical checks. Example demonstrates call with sample point and output t. Used in numerical irreducible decomposition contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: WitSupSet
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: WitSupSet(ideal I); I ideal. Return: list of Witness point Super Sets W(i) for i = 1,..,dim(V(I)), list L of generic linear polynomials and N(0) list of a polynomial system of same number of polynomials and unknowns. If W(i)=x then V(I) has no component of dimension i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute witness point supersets for components of each dimension. Example shows W(2), W(1), W(0) and L returned. These supersets are used to build witness sets for numerical decomposition; requires Bertini integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: WitSet
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: WitSet(ideal I); I ideal. Return: lists W(0..d) of witness point sets of i-dimensional components of V(J) for i=0..d (d=dim V(J)), and L list of generic linear polynomials. If W(i)=x then V(J) has no component of dimension i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: produce witness point sets (not just supersets) for numerical irreducible decomposition. Example shows using WitSet on a given ideal with returned W(1), W(0), L. Notes: witness sets are central to numerical decomposition pipeline and require Bertini.

rubrics_metrics.name: NumIrrDecom
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: NumIrrDecom(ideal I); Return: W = list of w(1),...,w(t) lists of irreducible witness point sets of irreducible components of V(J), with printed summary of dimensions and numbers of components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute numerical irreducible decomposition producing witness point sets for irreducible components of each dimension. Example output shows Dimension and Number of Components per dimension and how to access components via A(i)=W[i] and setring to inspect witness sets. Documentation shows how to interpret returned lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: defl
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: defl(ideal I, int d); I ideal, d order of the deflation. Return: deflation ideal DI of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute deflation ideal used to regularize singular components for numerical methods. Example shows defl(I,1) and setting ring to DI to inspect. Part of numerical decomposition toolkit.

rubrics_metrics.name: NumPrimDecom
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: NumPrimDecom(ideal I, int d); I ideal, d order of the deflation. Return: lists of the numerical primary decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute numerical primary decomposition up to deflation order d; returns witness sets for primary components. Example demonstrates calling NumPrimDecom(I,1) and inspecting resulting witness sets. Documentation cautions about example syntax and lack of test suite.

rubrics_metrics.name: tangentGens
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tangentGens(L, v); L list of strictly upper triangular n x n matrices, v matrix (n x 1). Assume: L generates a Lie algebra as vector space closed under Lie bracket; matrices are strictly upper triangular of same size; characteristic of base field either zero or > n when computing exponentials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list with four entries: [1] dimension of orbit of v under exp(<L>), [2] list of generators of tangent space to orbit at v (elements of <L>), [3] list of coefficient matrices expressing generators as combinations of L, [4] list of indices in v that can be made zero by action of exp(<L>). Theory: applies Chevalley-Rosenlicht theorem. Purpose: parametrize orbits of unipotent actions; examples provided showing output matrices.
